title: Stablecoin Weekly: Circle outpaces Tether, Latin America stirs, and banks move onchain
description: Stablecoin supply, holders, transfer activity and local-currency adoption.

blocks.text: @circle had the strongest week of any stablecoin issuer. USDC added $1.1B in market cap over the past seven days, roughly 2.5x Tether's USDT at $446.3M. At issuer level Circle grew by $1.0B, more than double @Tether’s $445.2M, even though Tether holds around 61% of total supply to Circle's 25%. Behind the two leaders, @SkyEcosystem added $151.8M through USDS, and @Ripple's RLUSD (+$112.6M) and @ethena’s USDe (+$107.7M) also passed $100M in growth.

blocks.text: Traditional banks are also starting to show up in the rankings. Crédit Agricole made the top 10 issuers, adding $39.0M through EURXT, the only euro stablecoin among the ten fastest-growing assets. Overall, though, dollar-pegged stablecoins still accounted for about 98% of all growth, adding $2.0B against $30.9M for euro stablecoins. Australian dollar, Japanese yen and Turkish lira stablecoins each added between $360K and $1.5M, while Canadian dollar and Mexican peso stablecoins dipped slightly. Total stablecoin supply now stands at $302.5B, up 1.4% over 30 days.

blocks.text: @BNBChain was far ahead on new wallets, adding 985K stablecoin holders, more than half of the top 10's total and almost 5x the next chain. @base came second with 202.5K, followed by @Celo at 168.9K and @trondao at 143.4K. Circle's new Arc chain added 109.1K holders in its early weeks, putting it ahead of both @solana and @arbitrum at around 100K each.

blocks.text: By asset, USDT added 845.9K new holders, about 62% of the top 10's holder growth, with USDC second at 390.8K. Circle's euro stablecoin EURC added 69.8K, the strongest showing of any non-dollar stablecoin. At issuer level, Tether (+814.2K) and Circle (+452.5K) together accounted for roughly 95% of new holders. After them growth falls away quickly: @Paxos added 21.8K, @phantom 18.6K, and @Polymarket made the list with 3.3K new holders of its pUSD stablecoin. Ethena stood out for the opposite reason, adding just 800 holders despite growing by more than $100M in market cap, which points to a small number of large holders rather than broad retail uptake.

blocks.text: The currency split for holders was just as lopsided. Dollar stablecoins added 1.3M holders and euro stablecoins 69.3K. Below those two, Latin America dominated: six of the top 10 currencies came from the region, led by the Argentine peso (+1.0K) and followed by the Chilean, Colombian and Mexican pesos, the Peruvian sol and the Brazilian real. The numbers are small, but they suggest local-currency stablecoins are starting to find users across LatAm.

blocks.text: Onchain activity was heavy all week, with $1.4T in stablecoins changing hands. DAI led transfer volume growth, up $2.4B, just ahead of RLUSD at $2.2B. That made Ripple the top issuer by transfer volume growth, more than 3x the next name. Euro stablecoins were again more active than their supply would suggest. EURXT added $610.2M in transfer volume, making Crédit Agricole the second-largest issuer by transfer growth. Fellow French bank Société Générale followed with $64.5M through EURCV, so two traditional banks made the top 10. @SoFi's SOFID and @LiquityProtocol's BOLD each added just over $100M, alongside newer names such as USDai, United Stables, Saturn and @lista_dao.
